the following questions: (a) How to construct aQR factorization of a matrixA, whereQ is an orthogonal matrix andR is upper triangular, (b) How to construct an orthogonal matrixQ that is close to orthogonal in the Frobenius norm, (c) How to construct such a matrixQ in a stable way, and (d) How to construct the orthogonal matrixQ and the upper triangular matrixR in a stable and efficient way.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the iterative modified algorithm is the best choice for constructing aQR decomposition, provided that one is interested in a matrixQ that approximates an orthogonal matrix in full working precision.
the iterative algorithms are the best ones to use for the computation of aQR factorization of a general rectangular matrix.
